Sensitivity analysis of a hypothetical land
use decision for smallholder farmers
in Kenya

supplementary material 2


Hannah Kamau

  • Objective
  • Control parameters
  • Base estimate and target correlation matrix
  • Iman–Conover induction + row-wise model application
  • Base correlated run and verification
  • Sensitivity A — correlation strength
  • Sensitivity B — project horizon (n_years)
  • Sensitivity C — discount rate
  • Combined grid — horizon × discount rate

Objective

Sensitivity analysis on the land_consolidation.R model. Three tests are done here

  • the assumption of independence (non-correlation)
  • varying the project horizon (n_years = 5, 10, 15, 20, 25) and
  • varying the discount rate (discount_rate = 5, 8, 10, 12, 15).
source("land_consolidation_function.R", encoding = "UTF-8")

Control parameters

base_nyears   <- 25
base_discount <- 10  # base discount rate (%) for one-at-a-time analyses 
nyear_grid    <- c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25) # sensitivity analysis B
discount_grid <- c(5, 8, 10, 12, 15) # sensitivity analysis C
corr_scales   <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5)   # sensitivity analysis A
# 0 = independent, 0.5 a weaker co-movement, 1 = assumed matrix, and 1.5 a stronger co-movement. (see later in the script)
n_runs_base <- 1e4
n_runs_grid <- 1e4 # per cell

Base estimate and target correlation matrix

Judgment based correlations

base_estimate <- decisionSupport::estimate_read_csv("land_consolidation_input.csv", sep = ";")

base_estimate$correlation_matrix <- NULL   # correlation is induced manually below

cor_vars <- c("maize_price_kes_kg", "production_costs_acre",
              "compensation_income_pm_acre", "hh_income_pa")

cor_mat <- matrix(c(
  1.00, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35, # source: judgment
  0.55, 1.00, 0.30, 0.20,
  0.45, 0.30, 1.00, 0.30,
  0.35, 0.20, 0.30, 1.00),
  nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(cor_vars, cor_vars)) 


stopifnot(all(eigen(cor_mat, only.values = TRUE)$values > 0))

Iman–Conover induction + row-wise model application

In 5 pieces i.e., draw the inputs, correlate them, push the inputs through the land_consolidation_function (model), and summarise the outputs. I apply Iman-Conover method (Iman and Conover 1982) which reorders the rows to match a set correlation target.

iman_conover <- function(X, target) {
  X <- as.matrix(X); n <- nrow(X); k <- ncol(X)
  a <- qnorm(seq_len(n) / (n + 1))                 # van der Waerden scores
  R <- sapply(seq_len(k), function(j) sample(a))   # random permutation per column
  P <- chol(cor(R))                                # cor(R) = t(P) %*% P  (upper)
  Q <- chol(target)
  Rstar <- R %*% solve(P) %*% Q                    # cor(Rstar) ~ target
  Y <- X
  for (j in seq_len(k)) {                          # reorder X to Rstar's rank pattern
    Y[, j] <- sort(X[, j])[rank(Rstar[, j], ties.method = "first")]
  }
  as.data.frame(Y)
}

# scale off-diagonals, keep valid & positive-definite
scale_cor <- function(m, s) {
  if (s == 0) return(NULL)
  od <- row(m) != col(m); m[od] <- pmin(pmax(m[od] * s, -0.95), 0.95)
  if (any(eigen(m, only.values = TRUE)$values <= 0))
    m <- as.matrix(Matrix::nearPD(m, corr = TRUE)$mat)
  m
}

# I prioritise KES scalar outputs of the model. The USD outputs and the
# vector output Cashflow_decision_do are deliberately excluded. KES is used to
# maintain the reporting in the manuscript.
scalar_out <- c("benefit_lc_kes", "benefit_status_quo_kes", "net_benefit_lc_kes")

# apply a `plainNames` model function row-by-row (returns the KES scalar outputs)
apply_model <- function(x, fn, keep = scalar_out) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(x)), function(i) {
    f <- fn
    environment(f) <- list2env(as.list(x[i, , drop = FALSE]), parent = globalenv())
    as.data.frame(f()[keep])
  }))
}

# draw independent marginals, induce correlation, run model -> net benefit (KES)
simulate_nb <- function(n_years_val = base_nyears, discount_val = base_discount,
                        target_cor = cor_mat, n_runs = n_runs_grid) {
  est <- base_estimate
  est$marginal["n_years", "distribution"]       <- "const"
  est$marginal["discount_rate", "distribution"] <- "const"
  for (col in intersect(c("lower", "median", "upper"), colnames(est$marginal))) {
    est$marginal["n_years", col]       <- n_years_val
    est$marginal["discount_rate", col] <- discount_val
  }
  x <- as.data.frame(decisionSupport::random(rho = est, n = n_runs, method = "calculate"))
  if (!is.null(target_cor)) x[cor_vars] <- iman_conover(x[cor_vars], target_cor)
  nb_total <- apply_model(x, land_consolidation_function)$net_benefit_lc_kes  # KES (per household)
  nb_total / x$ha_per_hh   # standardise to per hectare (KES/ha), as in the main analysis
}

summ <- function(nb, ...) data.frame(...,
  mean = mean(nb, na.rm = TRUE), median = median(nb, na.rm = TRUE),
  p5 = as.numeric(quantile(nb, .05, na.rm = TRUE)),
  p95 = as.numeric(quantile(nb, .95, na.rm = TRUE)),
  P_positive = mean(nb > 0, na.rm = TRUE), row.names = NULL)

Base correlated run and verification

Achieved rank correlation should approximate the target; marginals are preserved by construction.

xv <- as.data.frame(decisionSupport::random(rho = base_estimate, n = n_runs_base,
                                            method = "calculate"))
xv[cor_vars] <- iman_conover(xv[cor_vars], cor_mat)
cat("Target rank correlation:\n");   print(round(cor_mat, 2))
## Target rank correlation:
##                             maize_price_kes_kg production_costs_acre
## maize_price_kes_kg                        1.00                  0.55
## production_costs_acre                     0.55                  1.00
## compensation_income_pm_acre               0.45                  0.30
## hh_income_pa                              0.35                  0.20
##                             compensation_income_pm_acre hh_income_pa
## maize_price_kes_kg                                 0.45         0.35
## production_costs_acre                              0.30         0.20
## compensation_income_pm_acre                        1.00         0.30
## hh_income_pa                                       0.30         1.00
cat("\nAchieved rank correlation:\n"); print(round(cor(xv[cor_vars], method = "spearman"), 2))
## 
## Achieved rank correlation:
##                             maize_price_kes_kg production_costs_acre
## maize_price_kes_kg                        1.00                  0.53
## production_costs_acre                     0.53                  1.00
## compensation_income_pm_acre               0.43                  0.29
## hh_income_pa                              0.34                  0.19
##                             compensation_income_pm_acre hh_income_pa
## maize_price_kes_kg                                 0.43         0.34
## production_costs_acre                              0.29         0.19
## compensation_income_pm_acre                        1.00         0.28
## hh_income_pa                                       0.28         1.00
# the achieved Spearman correlations are below target by either -0.01 or -0.02. 
#  Nevertheless, this supports [@iman1982] as the MC reproduces the targeted rank correlation

nb_base <- simulate_nb(n_runs = n_runs_base)
summ(nb_base, case = "base (corr on, 25y, 10%)") %>%
  transmute(Case = case, Mean = fmt_m(mean), Median = fmt_m(median),
            `5th pct` = fmt_m(p5), `95th pct` = fmt_m(p95),
            `P(net benefit > 0)` = fmt_pct(P_positive)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Base case net benefit (million KES per hectare).", 
      booktabs = TRUE, align = "lrrrrr") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"),
                latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), full_width = FALSE)

Sensitivity A — correlation strength

sens_corr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(corr_scales, function(s)
  summ(simulate_nb(target_cor = scale_cor(cor_mat, s)), cor_scale = s)))

corr_labels <- c("0"   = "Independent (0×)",
                 "0.5" = "Half strength (0.5×)",
                 "1"   = "Assumed (1×)",
                 "1.5" = "Stronger (1.5×)")

sens_corr %>%
  transmute(
    `Input dependence`    = corr_labels[as.character(cor_scale)],
    `Mean`                = fmt_m(mean),
    `Median`              = fmt_m(median),
    `5th percentile`      = fmt_m(p5),
    `95th percentile`     = fmt_m(p95),
    `P(net benefit > 0)`  = fmt_pct(P_positive)
  ) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Net benefit of land consolidation (million KES per hectare) 
  under increasing variable correlation.",
      booktabs = TRUE, align = "lrrrrr", escape = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(1, width = "3.2cm") %>%
  footnote(
    general = paste0(
      "Net benefit = NPV(land consolidation) - NPV(maintain farms) = net_benefit_lc_kes, ",
      "reported in million KES per hectare, over a ", base_nyears, "-year horizon at a ",
      base_discount, "% discount rate. Correlations among maize price, production cost, ",
      "lease income and household income are induced with the Iman-Conover method. ",
      "Input dependence scales the off-diagonal entries of the assumed correlation matrix, ",
      "i.e. how strongly these four inputs co-move: Independent (0x) sets all pairwise ",
      "correlations to zero, so each input varies on its own; Half strength (0.5x) halves ",
      "the assumed correlations (weaker co-movement); Assumed (1x) applies the judgment-",
      "based target matrix; and Stronger (1.5x) inflates the assumed correlations ",
      "by 50% (stronger co-movement), bounded so the matrix remains valid and positive-definite. ",
      "Based on ", format(n_runs_grid, big.mark = ","),
      " Monte Carlo runs per row."),
    general_title = "Note. ", threeparttable = TRUE, footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)

Input dependence scales the off-diagonal entries of the assumed correlation matrix, i.e. how strongly these four inputs co-move: Independent (0x) sets all pairwise correlations to zero, so each input varies on its own; Half strength (0.5x) halves the assumed correlations (weaker co-movement); Assumed (1x) applies the judgment-based target matrix; and Stronger (1.5x) inflates the assumed correlations by 50% (stronger co-movement), bounded so the matrix remains valid and positive-definite. Based on 10,000 Monte Carlo runs per row.

Sensitivity B — project horizon (n_years)

sens_years <- do.call(rbind, lapply(nyear_grid, function(ny)
  summ(simulate_nb(n_years_val = ny), n_years = ny)))

sens_years %>%
  transmute(`Project horizon (years)` = n_years, Mean = fmt_m(mean), Median = fmt_m(median),
            `5th pct` = fmt_m(p5), `95th pct` = fmt_m(p95),
            `P(net benefit > 0)` = fmt_pct(P_positive)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Net benefit (million KES per hectare) vs project horizon.", booktabs = TRUE,
      align = "rrrrrr") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"),
                latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), full_width = FALSE)

Combined grid — horizon × discount rate

grid <- expand.grid(n_years = nyear_grid, discount_rate = discount_grid)
grid_res <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(ny, dr)
  summ(simulate_nb(ny, dr), n_years = ny, discount_rate = dr),
  grid$n_years, grid$discount_rate))

ggplot(grid_res, aes(factor(n_years), factor(discount_rate))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = median), colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(P_positive, accuracy = 1)), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "firebrick", mid = "white", high = "forestgreen",
                       midpoint = 0, labels = lab_m,
                       name = "Median net\nbenefit\n(million KES per hectare)") +
  labs(x = "Project horizon (years)", y = "Discount rate (%)",
       title = "When is land consolidation worthwhile?",
       subtitle = "Cell colour = median net benefit (million KES per hectare); 
       label = probability the net benefit is positive") +
  theme_minimal()

grid_res %>%
  transmute(`Horizon (years)` = n_years, `Discount rate (%)` = discount_rate,
            `Median net benefit (million KES per hectare)` = fmt_m(median),
            `P(net benefit > 0)` = fmt_pct(P_positive)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Full horizon x discount-rate grid (net benefit in million KES per hectare).",
      booktabs = TRUE, align = "rrrr") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"),
                latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), full_width = FALSE)
